root_cause.text: Incorrect clamping order in `vsock_update_buffer_size()` — clamping to the maximum before the minimum allows a user-set minimum larger than the maximum to override the maximum, enabling `vsk->buffer_size` to exceed `vsk->buffer_max_size` and violating memory boundary constraints.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff reverses the order from `max then min` to `min then max`, and the commit message explicitly states: "If a user sets a minimum buffer size larger than the maximum, the minimum check overrides the maximum check, inverting the constraint." The function `vsock_update_buffer_size()` in `net/vmw_vsock/af_vsock.c` is where the flawed logic resided.

candidates.rationale: This condition clamps val to the maximum, but due to ordering, it is applied before the minimum clamp, allowing the minimum to later override the maximum.
This assignment sets val to the maximum, but it can be overwritten by the subsequent minimum clamp if min > max, leading to val exceeding the maximum.
This condition checks if val is below the minimum; after the max clamp, if min > max, val is below min, triggering the override that allows val to exceed buffer_max_size.
This assignment sets val to the minimum, which can be larger than the maximum, violating the constraint that buffer_size should not exceed buffer_max_size.
This condition uses the potentially corrupted val to decide whether to notify, propagating the incorrect buffer size.
This notification call passes the corrupted val that may exceed buffer_max_size, leading to memory boundary violations when the transport uses it.
